sections.title: Basic Concept of Statistics
sections.content: Statistics involves the analysis of data. In Level 1, the main focus is on calculating Mean, Median, and Mode. Step 1: Read the data carefully. Step 2: Arrange the data in ascending order if required. Step 3: Apply the correct formula for Mean, Median, or Mode.

sections.title: Finding Mean
sections.content: Mean represents the average. Step 1: Add all the numbers. Step 2: Divide the sum by the total number of observations. Step 3: The result is the Mean. Example: Data = 5, 8, 12, 12, 15. Sum = 52. Total numbers = 5. Mean = 52/5 = 10.4.

sections.title: Finding Median
sections.content: Median is the middle value of the data set. Step 1: Arrange the data in ascending order. Step 2: Count the total number of observations. Step 3: If the number is odd, the middle value is the median. Step 4: If the number is even, take the average of the two middle numbers. Example: In 5, 8, 12, 12, 15 the median = 12.

sections.title: Finding Mode
sections.content: Mode is the value that appears most frequently in the data set. Step 1: Observe the data. Step 2: Identify the value that occurs the most times. Step 3: That value is the Mode. Example: In 5, 8, 12, 12, 15 the Mode = 12 because it appears twice.

sections.title: Change in Mean (Increase or Decrease)
sections.content: Step 1: If the same number is added to every observation, the mean increases by that number. Step 2: If the same number is subtracted from every observation, the mean decreases by that number. Step 3: If every observation is multiplied by a number, the mean is also multiplied by that number. Example: Mean = 20. If +5 is added to every value, the new mean = 25.

sections.title: Weighted Average
sections.content: Weighted average is used when different values have different importance. Step 1: Multiply each value by its weight. Step 2: Add all the products. Step 3: Divide by the total weight. Example: Marks 60, 70 and weights 2, 3. Weighted average = (60×2 + 70×3) / (2+3) = 330/5 = 66.

sections.title: Empirical Relationship
sections.content: An important relationship in statistics is: Mode = 3(Median) - 2(Mean). Step 1: Substitute the values of Median and Mean. Step 2: Apply the formula. Step 3: Calculate Mode. Example: Mean = 10, Median = 12. Mode = 3×12 - 2×10 = 36 - 20 = 16.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Not arranging the data before finding the median. 2. Failing to identify the most frequent value for mode. 3. Forgetting the weights in weighted average. 4. Incorrect substitution in the empirical formula.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Mean represents the average, Median represents the middle value, and Mode represents the most frequent value. In weighted average, weights must be considered carefully, and the empirical relationship can be used to find the mode.

tricks.title: Mean Quick Formula
tricks.explanation: Mean = Sum of all values / Total number of observations.

tricks.title: Median Shortcut
tricks.explanation: First arrange the data in ascending order, then pick the middle value.

tricks.title: Even Data Median Trick
tricks.explanation: If the number of observations is even, take the average of the two middle values.

tricks.title: Mode Identification Trick
tricks.explanation: The value that appears the most times is the Mode.

tricks.title: Constant Addition Rule
tricks.explanation: If k is added to every observation, the new mean = old mean + k.
tricks.example: Mean = 15, add +3 to every value → new mean = 18.

tricks.title: Constant Multiplication Rule
tricks.explanation: If every observation is multiplied by k, the mean is also multiplied by k.
tricks.example: Mean = 12, multiply every value by 2 → new mean = 24.

tricks.title: Weighted Average Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Weighted average = (sum of value × weight) / total weight.
